author: Ranjith Shivahari
title: Offer or
hook: price tag is not a promise!
simple_words: An offer can be accepted to make a contract. An invitation only asks others to make offers.

definitions.meaning: A person shows willingness to do or not do something, to get the other's assent, and intends to be bound on that assent.
definitions.note: Intention to be bound is the test

definitions.meaning: A step before an offer. The person invites others to make offers, and keeps the right to accept or refuse them.
definitions.note: Acceptance of it makes no contract

key_points: An offer needs ==intention to be bound== once the other party accepts
Goods with price tags, price lists, catalogues and ==tender notices== are invitations
At an auction, the announcement invites; the ==bid is the offer==, accepted by fall of hammer
!!A general offer (reward advertisement) is a real offer!!, accepted by performing the condition

rows: No contract; only an offer follows
Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball Co.

insight.text: In a shop, the customer offers to buy at the tag price, and the shopkeeper accepts at the counter.

memory_trick.explanation: The shop window or catalogue only shows goods (invitation). The customer's hand at the counter makes the offer; the seller's yes is acceptance.

steps: Ask: intends to be bound on yes?
Check for a general offer reward
exam_tip: In an MCQ, a price tag, catalogue, tender notice or auction announcement means invitation to offer. A reward advertisement means offer.

doubt.question: Is a shopkeeper bound to sell at the displayed price?
doubt.answer: No. The display is an invitation. The customer's request to buy is the offer, and the shopkeeper may accept or refuse it.

mistakes_hook: don't fall for the price tag

mistakes.wrong: Price tag on goods is an offer, so shop must sell
mistakes.right: A price tag is an invitation to offer. The customer makes the offer.

mistakes.wrong: Tender notice is an offer; bidder accepts it
mistakes.right: The notice invites tenders. The tender submitted is the offer.
The announcement is an invitation. The bid is the offer.

mistakes.wrong: Reward advertisement is only an invitation
mistakes.right: It is a general offer, accepted by performing the condition (Carlill case).

reviewer_note: Check S.2(a) reference and that case names match the ICAI study material. Auction rule assumes no reserve or special terms.

Checker 1: Step 1 ('Find who speaks first') is vague and could mislead: the party who speaks first often makes only an invitation (shop display, tender notice, auction announcement). Better: 'Identify the first statement or act and who made it, then test whether it is an offer or only an invitation.'
Checker 1: Table row 5, Offer column ('Seller or buyer') is correct but terse. Clearer: 'Either party, seller or buyer (e.g. promisor in a reward advertisement)'.
